BiblicalUsage: There is famine in the land, and Abram goes down into Egypt; the seven years of dearth come on all lands, and Joseph's Egypt has bread. Hunger and thirst and nakedness are the curse for disobedience, and Amos warns of a famine not of bread nor of thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe famine is God's instrument and his provision both, because the same hunger that drove Abram to Egypt brought Joseph's brothers to the grain. I hold that the worst famine is not of bread but of hearing the word of the LORD, and Amos says that day is coming.
RelatedTopics: Judgment; God's Provision; Word of God
